findings.location: <harness-onion>/architecture/review-record/README.md, 'The merge', 'A VOID round (Q-RR2-VOID (b), the monitor's ruling)'; <harness-onion>/scripts/review_record.py _series_matches, _overlap
findings.finding: The new VOID paragraph says: 'To recover, the lane opens a new series id for the rerun, which needs a registry entry and so the owner's per-PR approval'. That holds only when the series is registered by an exact id. The registry also takes prefix entries (the README's 'a prefix such as MET-GOV-002/'), and _series_matches matches any series id that starts with the prefix. B-3's overlap rule even refuses an added exact entry under an existing prefix. So under a prefix entry, a rerun series id needs no registry change and no new owner approval. Probe 2, on the vectors' base registry: a round with the new series id EXAMPLE-002/rerun, under the prefix entry EXAMPLE-002/, passes both check_review and check_series. Under the published exact entry MET-GOV-002/contract, MET-GOV-002/contract-rerun is BRIEF_NOT_FOR_SERIES. The monitor chose (b) over (a) because (b) keeps the owner gate on recovery, so the README overstates that gate for prefix-registered series. This packet's own series is registered by exact id, so it is not affected now.
findings.requiredChange: State the prefix case in the VOID paragraph. Under an exact-id entry, the rerun's new series id needs a registry entry and so the owner's per-PR approval. Under a prefix entry, a new id under that prefix is already covered, so the only owner gate is the earlier approval of the prefix. Flag this to the monitor with the fix. If the owner gate on recovery should also hold for prefix entries, that needs a monitor or owner rule; it is not a change to (b).
